name: Banners
title: Storefront banners in Go (GoCommerce module)
description: Keep a GoCommerce storefront’s home page pictures as rows: slides across the top, grids of tiles under a heading, a phone picture, a switch and one saved order.
ogDescription: Slides and grids of tiles for the home page, one row per picture, served already split for the storefront.
lede: A Go package that keeps the pictures on a storefront’s home page as rows, one per picture: slides across the top, and grids of tiles under a heading. Each is a picture, an optional phone picture, a title that is also its alternative text, and a link. The storefront reads them at /x/banners?page=home, already split into slides and grids.
what: In the package’s own words, banners are “the pictures a shop puts on its storefront’s pages: slides across the top of a page, and grids of tiles under a heading, each a picture and a link.” They are kept as rows, one per picture, so a shop adds, reorders and switches off one banner without rewriting a page.

A banner has a placement, slide or grid, and a grid tile has a heading: tiles with the same heading on a page form one grid. The picture is wide enough for a desktop; an optional narrower crop is for phones, and without one the wide picture is used there too. The order is the shop’s own and runs across the whole page.

Each banner names its page, so other pages can follow, but only the home page is accepted until a storefront shows banners anywhere else. A store that starts with the sample shop gets three slides and a Shop by collection grid, made from the sample shop’s photographs.
configLede: There is nothing to set in Go: Config is an empty struct, there so a setting can arrive without changing how the module is installed. Banners are rows an operator edits on the admin’s Content › Banners screen or through the API.

config.note: The plugin’s switch, on by default. Off, GET /x/banners answers 404 while the Banners screen and its admin routes keep working, so banners can be prepared before they show.

setup.t: Pass banners.New to gocommerce.New, as below, or start the reference binary with -banners. It adds one table.
On Content › Banners, add a slide or a grid tile: a picture chosen from Files or typed in as a link, an optional phone picture, a title and a link such as /collections/new-in.
Move banners with the arrows on the screen. The page’s whole order is saved at once, with PUT /api/admin/x/banners/order.
The storefront reads GET /x/banners?page=home and gets slides and grids, each grid with its heading and its tiles in order. Only switched-on banners are served.

codeNote: The package doc has no example of its own; this is how the reference binary’s -banners flag installs it. cfg is your gocommerce.Config.

howItWorks.t: GET /x/banners?page=home answers the page, its slides and its grids, with only switched-on banners and in the shop’s order. Grids come in the order their first tile appears. Each banner carries its id, title, link, picture and phone picture.

PUT /api/admin/x/banners/order takes every banner on the page, each once, and rewrites their positions in one transaction. An order that leaves one out or names one twice is refused, so a page is never half sorted. A new banner goes last on its page.

A picture or a link is a path on the site or an http or https address. javascript:, data:, a protocol-relative //host, /\ and any whitespace or control character are refused. Addresses are at most 2,048 characters, titles 200.

howItWorks.b: A switch that keeps the banner
howItWorks.t: Switching a banner off takes it off the storefront without deleting it. A save that does not mention the switch leaves it as it was.
banners.read for managers and staff, banners.write for managers: changing what every visitor sees on arrival is the manager’s.

howItWorks.b: Sample banners come and go together
howItWorks.t: The sample shop’s slides and grid are marked as samples, which only the engine sets, and are erased with the rest of the sample shop. A slide whose sample collection or category the store lacks is left out rather than linking nowhere.

limits.t: A banner for any page but home is refused. The column is there for other pages; the storefront shows banners on its home page alone.
A banner is on or off. There is no start or end date; the switch is the only way to time one.
The module stores the picture’s address. Uploading is the Files screen’s job, and the module does not check that a picture exists or how large it is.
Slides and grid tiles. There are no other layouts, and a tile’s grid is known only by its heading text.
Nothing records how often a banner was seen or clicked.

faq.a: GET /x/banners?page=home on the host that serves your GoCommerce API. It answers the page name, a list of slides and a list of grids, each grid with its heading and tiles, already in the shop’s order.

faq.q: Can a banner show on a collection page?
faq.a: No. Only the home page is accepted, because no storefront shows banners anywhere else yet.
No. A banner has an on and off switch and no dates. Switch it on when it should show, and off afterwards.

faq.q: What size should the pictures be?
faq.a: The module does not say or check. It takes a wide picture for desktops and an optional narrower one for phones; without the phone picture the wide one is used on phones too.
